about: A map of what MeteoAlarm publishes for machines, made by following its own pages and links: every address here is one MeteoAlarm documents or links to, or one its public website was seen to call. Nothing was guessed in bulk. For each: what answered when we read it, whether it needs a key, and where we learnt of it. One request every three seconds, a plain client name. Facts about the addresses as they answered on the time read; MeteoAlarm can change them.

hosts.what: the public website: the map of Europe, the pages (terms, FAQ, warning providers and consumers, redistribution hub), an archive view
the open feeds: an Atom feed per country and, under /api/v1/warnings/, the same as JSON
the API portal: OGC EDR v1.0.0, MQTT v1.0.0, Metadata v0.1, Hub v1.0.0
the test system, "completely decoupled from the production system" (EDR FAQ)

endpoints.returns: {warnings: [{uuid, alert: {identifier, sender, sent, status, msgType, scope, references, incidents, info: [one block per language: event, headline, description, onset, effective, expires, severity, certainty, urgency, responseType, category, senderName, web, parameter[awareness_level, awareness_type], area[areaDesc, geocode[EMMA_ID]]]}}]}
endpoints.notes: No paging, no query parameters documented. Sends no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header (a browser on another site cannot read it). Holds expired messages for days: on 11 Nov 02:14 the oldest was sent 6 Nov 07:14. A message replaced by an Update is usually dropped, but stays listed when the Update's reference is written with a stray dash (seen from IPMA): follow references, not only expiry.

endpoints.notes: Its bytes were the same across our five reads between 02:14 and 02:27 UTC (its updated stamp read 02:05): the feed is rebuilt from time to time, not on every request. Fewer entries than the JSON has messages (122 against 191 at the same minute): it appears to leave out what has expired (our reading, not MeteoAlarm's statement).

history.question: Does MeteoAlarm keep the warnings it has dropped from the open feed (for us: Madeira's on Tuesday 10 November, 12:00 to 21:00 UTC)?
history.answer: Yes, by its own description: the EDR API serves "realtime and archived weather warnings" and "historical data can be queried"; the website has an archive view. The open feed does not: a replaced message is gone from it (the 11 Nov 02:14 read holds no Madeira message whose hours touch Tuesday 12:00 to 21:00). Reaching the archive needs a token from MeteoAlarm (for re-distributors) or a free MeteoGate key (for the public). We have neither.
history.label: the two quoted statements are facts read from MeteoAlarm's pages; that the missing Madeira messages are in the archive is a hypothesis until someone queries it
